workouts.title: SPUS 1.1 (Week 1, Workout 1)
workouts.description: Welcome to Strict Pull-Up Strength! Today we’re setting your baseline for the program, so be sure to video all three check in attempts. This will help you track your progress over the next 8 weeks. If you don’t have any pull-ups yet, don’t stress! That’s exactly why you’re here. Measuring progress is important, so complete your check in today and you’ll be glad you did when we look back later. We’re also introducing tempo training, a method that builds strength by slowing things down and increasing time under tension. In your Banded Face Pulls today, the tempo @1111 means each part of the movement takes 1 second. It’s not about rushing, it’s about moving with control and intention.

Max Unbroken Strict Chest to Bar Pull-up Attempt

workouts.title: SPUS 1.2 (Week 1, Workout 2)
workouts.description: Today we’re focusing on hanging, the foundation of a strong pull-up. Don’t overlook the importance of proper hand placement and active engagement. Building good habits here sets you up for long-term progress and injury-free pulling.

items.movement: 20sec x Pronated Passive Hang + 10sec x Pronated Active Hang

workouts.title: SPUS 1.3 (Week 1, Workout 3)
workouts.description: Let’s get to work on building upper body pulling strength! Today is all about repeating one key pattern: stack the shoulders down and back, then pull. Drill that in every rep. We’re also adding a bit more complexity with tempo work. For example, in a movement like Trap 3 Raise @2106, that means: wait 1 sec before you lift immediately (0), hold at the top for 6 seconds, then lower over 2 seconds. If you need a refresher on tempo, review Lesson 1 or ask in the Academy coaching space, we’re here to help.

workouts.title: SPUS 2.1 (Week 2, Workout 1)
workouts.description: Today’s session is all about grip and hanging strength. There’s a lot of volume coming your way, so stick to the rest times, stay focused, and hang on tight!

workouts.title: SPUS 2.2 (Week 2, Workout 2)
workouts.description: Today is all about the pulling pattern. Elbow flexion strength plays a key role in your ability to perform pull-ups and is also essential for keeping your elbows and shoulders healthy. Stay focused, put in the work, and enjoy the process. A quick note on today’s movements: Dumbbell External Rotations should not be heavy. If you don’t have light dumbbells, use fractional plates or any small object you can hold comfortably. For Bicep Curls, choose a load that’s challenging but controllable.

workouts.title: SPUS 2.3 (Week 2, Workout 3)
workouts.description: In today’s session, we’re introducing a few different grip positions in your pulling work. Remember, your shoulder blades should stay in the same stacked position, down and away from your ears. Any grip rotation should come through the elbow, not the shoulder. Below is a quick breakdown of the different grips you’ll be using. Check out the corresponding demo videos to see each grip in action.

workouts.title: SPUS 3.1 (Week 3, Workout 1)
workouts.description: Today we’re introducing the lowering (eccentric) phase of the pull-up. A powerful tool for building strength and control. Use a pull-up bar that’s high enough for your feet to hang freely without needing to tuck. A sturdy box is recommended to help you get into the assisted position, noted as the “A” in the @51A1 tempo. Control is key. Lower yourself all the way to a passive hang and avoid dropping into the bottom position. If that’s too challenging, use a box that allows you to start at the top, then use your legs (typically your toes) to assist the descent. Make it challenging! The goal is to gradually reduce leg assistance and eventually eliminate the box altogether.

items.movement: 2-3 x Supinated Pull-up Negative (5 seconds down)
Scale to Box Assisted Pull-Up Negatives instead.

workouts.title: SPUS 3.2 (Week 3, Workout 2)
workouts.description: Just like last week, today is all about refining the pull pattern. Elbow flexion is key not only for building toward your first pull-up but also for maintaining healthy elbows and shoulders. Put in the work and enjoy the progress!

workouts.title: SPUS 3.3 (Week 3, Workout 3)
workouts.description: Your grip may be challenged today with the introduction of Powell Raises, an excellent exercise for strengthening your shoulders, along with some valuable time spent in the passive hang. Stay focused, stay engaged, and hang out in your happy place.

items.movement: 1 min x Pronated Grip Ring Row
Accumulate 1 min in minimal sets x Pronated Passive Hang

workouts.title: SPUS 4.1 (Week 4, Workout 1)
workouts.description: We’re already at the halfway point! Today we continue progressing through our controlled negatives. Keep a close eye on your tempo and stay sharp with your positions!

items.movement: 2-3 x Pronated Pull-up Negative (5 seconds down)

workouts.title: SPUS 4.2 (Week 4, Workout 2)
workouts.description: You’ve put in the work to dial in proper shoulder position at the start of your pull-up. Today, it’s time to start bending those arms! Focus on driving the movement by using your back to pull up and not just your arms.

workouts.title: SPUS 4.3 (Week 4, Workout 3)
workouts.description: You’ve been working hard on your pulling pattern, and now it’s time to get into some bent-arm hanging. Remember, your shoulders have no business touching your ears. Avoid a shrugging pattern at all costs. Think shoulder bladed back and down, that’s the name of the game!

items.movement: Chin Over Bar Hold too challenging?
Use a box or bands to assist the hold

workouts.title: SPUS 5.1 (Week 5, Workout 1)
workouts.description: It’s time to check in on your progress and get some pull-up attempts in! No matter the results, you’re on the right path! Keep showing up and putting in the work. Remember to video your check-in attempts. These are invaluable for tracking your progress, sharing with WODprep Coaches, and reviewing on your own. You might even spot a few faults from the Fault Fixer series that could be holding you back. Keep grinding, you’ve got this!

workouts.title: SPUS 5.2 (Week 5, Workout 2)
workouts.description: After the last lesson, you should have a solid sense of where you are in your pull-up progress and milestones. Hopefully, your videos helped highlight a few key focus areas. Bring that insight into today’s session, stay intentional, and enjoy the work. This is where real progress is made!

workouts.title: SPUS 5.3 (Week 5, Workout 3)
workouts.description: Today we are attacking some load sequencing faults and bent arm static holds. It’s all about understanding, and movement fluency. Be present and focused in on every little activation through these movements today.

items.movement: Chin Over Bar Hold too challenging?
Use a box or bands to assist the hold

workouts.title: SPUS 6.1 (Week 6, Workout 1)
workouts.description: Can you keep an active midline while you pull? If not, you’re not performing your strict pull-up as efficiently as possible. After today’s session, and with the help of some new drills. you’ll gain a better understanding of just how important midline stability is throughout the pull.

items.movement: 5 x Single Leg Assisted Strict Pull-up @2121
1 x Pronated Pull-up Negative (5sec down) + 5 x Scapular Pull-up

workouts.title: SPUS 6.2 (Week 6, Workout 2)
workouts.description: We’ve got a high-volume session today with 10 sets of 10 Inverted Ring Rows. If maintaining proper form for all 10 reps is too tough, scale back to standard ring rows. Prioritize quality over quantity, and make sure you’re giving yourself enough recovery afterwards. A good night’s rest or even an extra rest day before the next session, will go a long way in supporting your progress.

items.movement: 10 x Inverted Ring Row (feet on box)
Modify to regular ring rows with a more challenging foot position.

workouts.title: SPUS 6.3 (Week 6, Workout 3)
workouts.description: Today we’re bringing out the bands to help you feel the full concentric portion of the pull-up with reduced load. Choose a band that challenges you for the required volume, and don’t forget everything you’ve learned about positioning. Stay focused and stick to solid form!

items.movement: Pronated Pull-up Negative (5sec down) + 6 x Scapular Pull-up @2222
Use as many bands as needed to consistently achieve 5–10 quality pull-ups.

workouts.title: SPUS 7.1 (Week 7, Workout 1)
workouts.description: There’s a lot of volume in today’s negative reps, so stay sharp. Avoid dropping into the bottom uncontrolled. Stick to the tempo, stay engaged, and use your back throughout every rep! SKILLS 8 min EMOM: Min 1: 2 x Pronated Pull-up Negative @11A5 + 6x Scapular Pull-up @2222 Min 2: 30-40sec x Hollow Body Band Pulldown @2222 + 4 Sets 6-8 x Single Leg Assisted Strict Pull-up @2121 2-4 x Pronated Pull-up Negative (6 seconds down)

workouts.title: SPUS 7.2 (Week 7, Workout 2)
workouts.description: Today is all about building pulling strength. Make sure your rows and curls are performed at a challenging weight. Enough to push you, while still maintaining good form.

workouts.title: SPUS 7.3 (Week 7, Workout 3)
workouts.description: Keep that core tight! We’re challenging midline stability again today, so make sure every rep is controlled and truly challenging. Quality over quantity!

workouts.title: SPUS 8.1 (Week 8, Workout 1)
workouts.description: The final week of Strict Pull-Up Strength is here! Let’s finish strong with some a demanding drills to set you up for showcasing all your hard work in the final session.

items.movement: 3-5 x Pronated Pull-up Negative (8 seconds down)
6-8 x Single Leg Assisted Strict Pull-up @2121
Chin Over Bar Hold too challenging?
Use a box or bands to assist the hold

workouts.title: SPUS 8.2 (Week 8, Workout 2)
workouts.description: We’ve got a lot of pulling on the menu today, so find the balance between challenging yourself and maintaining proper form. Aim for quality over quantity as we head into the final day!

items.movement: Left Single Arm Supinated Bicep Curl @50X0
Right Single Arm Supinated Bicep Curl @50X0

workouts.title: SPUS 8.3 (Week 8, Workout 3)
workouts.description: It’s here, the final day of Strict Pull-Up Strength! Today, we put all your hard work to the test with a check-in on your strict pull-up progress. For some, that might mean hitting a big PR. For others, it could be improved shapes, stronger positions, or simply getting your chin a little closer to the bar. No matter what your check-in numbers look like, we’re proud of the effort you’ve put in. We want to celebrate your success! Post your before-and-after videos on the Wall of Wins and earn yourself with some sweet WODprep swag just for sharing.
